meta_title: VpnHood! SERVER: Open-Source VPN Server for Linux & Windows
meta_description: Free, open-source VPN server for Linux, Windows and Docker. VpnHood! MANAGER installs it for you, or one command does. TCP, UDP, QUIC and Cloak Mode.
page_title: VpnHood! SERVER: free, open-source VPN server software
page_desc: The engine of your VPN. It runs on your own machine, carries your users' traffic, and answers to nobody's infrastructure but yours.
f_anywhere_desc: Linux (x64 or ARM64), Windows, or Docker, on a VPS or dedicated machine that meets its system requirements. VpnHood! MANAGER installs it for you, or you paste a single command. It listens on port 443 out of the box, with no network configuration.
f_stealth_title: Hard to spot, harder to block
f_stealth_desc: With Cloak Mode, the tunnel is shaped to look like ordinary web traffic, and an unauthenticated probe gets a plain web-server response instead of anything worth testing. No network is guaranteed to let it through, but there is little to match against.
f_engine_desc: VpnHood! ENGINE keeps the connection encrypted and stable across hostile networks, over TCP, UDP and QUIC, with IPv4 and IPv6 support.
f_open_desc: Every line is public on GitHub under the LGPL, and the project has been audited by Include Security for the Open Technology Fund's Red Team Lab. Nothing to take on faith.
cta: Free, open-source, and ready for your server.
hero_alt: A server rack on a plinth, a shielded tunnel leaving it, and three small device screens connecting back to it
prod_desc: The details that decide whether a VPN server is something you set up once or something you babysit.
prod_1: Restart or update the server and open sessions carry on.
prod_2: It does not need administrator rights, and on Linux it can run without root at all.
prod_3: Users who try to scan networks through your server are stopped, which keeps your IP out of abuse reports.
prod_4: Works behind Cloudflare and the like, and still sees each client's real IP.
prod_5: With MANAGER, each plan sets how much traffic its keys get and how fast it moves.
run_note: Either way, your users connect with VpnHood! CLIENT, free on Android, iOS, Apple TV, Windows and Linux. Your own white-labelled app can connect to the same servers.
install_desc: Let VpnHood! MANAGER do it for you, or paste one command and run the server standalone.
install_manager_title: Let VpnHood! MANAGER install it for you
install_manager_desc: Add your server in MANAGER and give it the machine's SSH login: MANAGER installs, configures and starts VpnHood! SERVER, then issues your access keys. Rather not share a login? It shows you one command to paste instead. Add more servers later, and MANAGER balances your users across them.
install_solo_desc: A standalone server needs no panel. Paste one line on a fresh Linux machine: it installs the service, configures it and starts it. Then ask it for your first access key.
install_guide: Full setup guide for Linux, Docker and Windows
